answer: A stake-backed trellis of mutual vouching resists sybils: each agent must lock a deposit and earn vouches from established peers before trading, so a fake identity costs real funds plus the time to build trust. Peers echo only vouched credentials, and any identity caught cloning another loses its deposit and its plume of reputation at once. Creating 1,000 fakes would cost 1,000 deposits and weeks of vouched history, while honest agents pay once.
